root.name: Queen's Indian Defense: Averbakh Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. e3 Bb7 5. Bd3 c5 6. O-O Be7 7. b3 O-O 8. Bb2 cxd4 9. Nxd4

overview: White has traded on d4 and recaptured with the knight, with the bishops on b2 and d3 aimed at the kingside. Black has ...c5 played, a half-open c-file and a solid ...d6 or ...Nc6 build-up. Play is balanced and manoeuvring.

white_ideas.idea: Rc1, Qe2 and Nd2, with f4 or e4 expansion
Bishop on b2 supports pressure along the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Use the c-file and ...Rc8 for counterplay

typical_structures.structure: Asymmetric centre with a half-open c-file for Black, White pawns on e3 and b3

character.notes: Neither sharp nor especially hard to break: a manoeuvring fight over the c-file.

soundness.notes: A normal main-line Queen's Indian set-up.

structure.notes: The d-pawn is gone, so Black has a half-open c-file in an asymmetric centre.

level.notes: Plans matter more than long forcing lines.
